title: The screening cascade: a wide net, a queue of the team's capacity with an audit, confirmed labels back into a model, recall per stage
request: Phase 8 (the owner's pattern 3): two-stage screening, high recall first and then precision; a case summary for reviewers that is advisory and off for private projects; a review queue sized by capacity K with a random audit sample; confirmed labels back into a supervised leaf; recall measured per stage.
plan: Read the retail returns replica (capacity five a day, the late-evening rule, copied bills, drift) and the capacity module of 30.12.
Write the cascade as a day-by-day simulation in dclab_core: the net, the queue and its audit, the labels back, the summaries.
Run it on the replica's three seeds with the learning on and off; keep every run whole beside its record.
Review it adversarially, fix what it finds, and measure again.

decisions.decision: The cascade is simulated day by day, each day's rows screened when the day is known.
decisions.why: Recall per stage is only honest if no stage reads a later day: the anomaly medians, the links and the model are fitted on what came before.

decisions.decision: The reviewers are a mapping asked about one reviewed row at a time; a replica's truth for measuring is a separate argument read after the run.
decisions.why: Nothing may read a row's outcome before a reviewer confirms it; the test's reviewers refuse every other way of reading.

decisions.decision: The net's anomaly part is a share of the day's rows (0.15), measured: about half the rows and nine cases in ten.
decisions.why: A fixed multiple of K took every row of the replica's small days, so the net was no stage at all.

decisions.decision: The audit's interval also bounds what the rows left by a stage may hold.
decisions.why: An audit that finds no case among the rows a queue left says little when it saw a few dozen of over a thousand.

decisions.decision: The programme template (the cascade as a Programme the studio runs on a project) is left for a later package.
decisions.why: The Programme's protocol is fit, validation and one holdout read; the cascade's is days with labels fed back: making them one path is a design of its own.

change: dclab_core.cascade (run, NET_SHARE, MIN_POSITIVES, STAGES); dclab_core.capacity.audit_recall's bound on missed cases; dclab_rnd.cascade (links_of, replica_run, run, write, detail, the CLI); tests/test_cascade.py; dclab-core 0.93.0; pattern 3 built.

findings.scenario: A bill's first return was flagged as returned twice on its own day because the same bill came back later: half the flagged rows on every seed.
findings.cause: returned_twice was a duplicated() count over the whole log.
findings.fix: Counted over the returns of the bill on that day or earlier.

findings.defect: The wide net was not a stage.
findings.scenario: The anomaly part took the top twenty rows of a day with nineteen: the net held 98.6% of the holdout's rows and recall one by construction.
findings.cause: The net's size was a multiple of K, larger than most days.
findings.fix: A share of the day's rows, measured on three seeds: about half the rows, recall 0.91 to 0.99; the net's share of rows reported.

findings.defect: The audit's interval left out the true recall.
findings.scenario: Seed 1: estimate 1.0, interval 0.959 to 1.0, true queue recall 0.891.
findings.cause: With no audited case among the rows the queue left, every bootstrap draw read one, and Kish's count saw only the queue's own cases.
findings.fix: capacity.audit_recall bounds the uncaught rows' cases by Wilson's interval on the audited ones times their number, and takes the wider interval.

findings.defect: The case summary received the label and the review's verdict.
findings.scenario: A recorded call to summarize held label, label_source, review_status and a rule computed with the future.
findings.cause: Every column of the frame was passed, and the replica's frame kept the outcome columns.
findings.fix: A summary sees only what screening reads; the replica drops the label and its kept-out columns; a column in keep_out is refused as anything read; a private project is never summarised by a model.

findings.defect: Summaries were cut to 600 characters before they were kept.
findings.scenario: A 1000-character summary was stored as 600; a failing summary left no trace; why was lost when a model's words replaced the template.
findings.cause: A display cut applied before capture.
findings.fix: Each queued case kept whole: its summary, source, why, error, risk, learned and anomaly scores and day.

findings.defect: Every summary said the learned model ranked the row high.
findings.scenario: 836 of 1064 summaries on seed 0 carried the reason, whatever the row's learned rank.
findings.cause: The reason was attached whenever a model existed.
findings.fix: Said only of a row among the model's highest of the day.

findings.defect: The anomaly medians were fitted on all days before the holdout.
findings.scenario: An early day was scored with medians that held later days.
findings.fix: Refitted every round on the days before; the first day on its own batch, known at screening.

findings.defect: The test of reads watched only one way of reading the outcomes.
findings.scenario: A read through review[k], in or items() would have passed, and adding the label to the features passed every test.
findings.cause: The test's reviewers overrode get only; nothing refused a kept-out column.
findings.fix: The test's reviewers refuse every other access; run refuses keep_out columns.

measurements.name: the screening cascade on the retail returns replica (CSC-001, from committed code)
measurements.gate: the plan's Done when: recall per stage measured on the latest period, the learning against no learning on the same seeds, the audit's interval covering the true recall, the summary never changing a label
measurements.result: net recall 0.908, 0.950, 0.990 on seeds 0 to 2 with 0.507 to 0.527 of the rows; queue recall 0.759, 0.861, 0.907 against 0.724, 0.822, 0.804 with the learning off; queue precision 0.183 to 0.245; the audit's intervals from about 0.43 to 0.60 up to 1.0, each covering the truth
limits: Invented data: the replica's truth stands for reviewers who are always right.
The replica's team reviews far more of the holdout's rows than a real team would.
One audit row a day: the intervals are wide.

outcome: DCLab screens a stream of cases as a team of K would, says what each stage catches with an interval that covers the truth, learns from what the team confirms, and keeps each case's summary whole and advisory.
lessons: A stage sized by a constant can swallow a small day whole: size it by the day and report what it keeps.
An interval tested only where its estimator is easy hides where it is wrong: check it against a truth on every seed.
risks: The cascade is not yet a Programme the studio runs on a project; the anomaly review loop and it are two paths.
The replica's team reviews a quarter of the rows, far more than a real team: its recall says the method works, not what a real queue catches.
No model wrote a summary yet: no gateway purpose serves it.
